USACE HEC-HMS Technical Reference: Modified USLE

limitations: Screens whether erosion-mediated particle transport is plausible; it does not estimate concentration, dose, risk, or regulatory acceptability.
Classification depends on user-supplied physicochemical evidence and coarse substance-class cues.
profiles.applicability_note: Use before RUSLE/MUSLE when deciding whether sediment-associated transport is relevant for a soil release scenario.

profiles.display_name: Modified Universal Soil Loss Equation event sediment-yield estimate
profiles.equation_text: Sed = 11.8 * (Qsurf * qpeak)^0.56 * K * LS * C * P

source_references.title: USACE HEC-HMS Technical Reference: Modified USLE

limitations: Requires caller-provided runoff volume and peak runoff rate.
Does not compute rainfall-runoff generation, hydrologic routing, calibration, receiving-water dilution, exposure, or risk.
profiles.applicability_note: Use MUSLE when event runoff and peak-flow information are already available and a scalar sediment-yield screen is needed.

profiles.display_name: Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation screening estimate
profiles.equation_text: A = R * K * LS * C * P

source_references.title: USDA NRCS Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation guidance

limitations: Returns long-term average annual soil loss for scalar screening.
Does not estimate event sediment yield, channel routing, deposition, receiving-water concentration, exposure, or risk.
profiles.applicability_note: Use RUSLE for erosion susceptibility or gross soil-loss screening when explicit R, K, LS, C, and P factors are available.

source_references.title: USACE HEC-HMS Technical Reference: Modified USLE

limitations: Uses explicit caller-provided delivery and availability fractions.
Returns load only; it does not estimate receiving-water concentration, dose, exposure, risk, or regulatory acceptability.
profiles.applicability_note: Use after MUSLE or another sediment-yield estimate when a bounded sediment-associated chemical-load handoff is needed.

source_references.title: USDA NRCS Water Erosion Prediction Project

limitations: WEPP is not executed, reimplemented, or claimed equivalent inside this update.
Future support should validate, run or ingest externally generated WEPP scenarios/results, then normalize outputs into bounded MCP contracts with provenance.
deferred_capabilities: run WEPP when an operator-managed executable or service is configured
import WEPP output with version, parameter, and limitation provenance
profiles.applicability_note: Treat WEPP as a future external-model adapter path for process-based hillslope or small-watershed erosion simulation.
